title: Parsing command-line arguments
description:
The final project reads options like `--level warn --top 3 --source auth`. Write the parser:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
enum Level { Debug, Info, Warn, Error }               // in order of severity

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Options { level: Level, top: usize, sources: Vec<String>, help: bool }

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum ArgError { Unknown(String), MissingValue(String), BadValue { option: String, value: String } }

impl std::str::FromStr for Level                       // "debug", "INFO", "Warn"... (any case); Err(()) otherwise
impl std::fmt::Display for ArgError
fn parse_args(args: &[&str]) -> Result<Options, ArgError>
```

- Defaults: level `Debug` (everything), top 5, no sources, help false.
- `--level <level>`, `--top <n>` (a whole number of 1 or more), `--source <name>` (may be given several times; collected in order), `-h`/`--help`. The value can also be written `--top=3`.
- Errors: an unknown argument gives `Unknown(arg)`; an option without a value `MissingValue(option)`; a bad level or number `BadValue`.
- Messages: `unknown argument '<arg>'`, `<option> needs a value`, `invalid value '<value>' for <option>`.
hints: Walk the arguments with an index so an option can take the next argument as its value; `arg.split_once('=')` handles the `--top=3` form.
Deriving `PartialOrd` and `Ord` on `Level` orders the variants as written, so "at least warn" is simply `level >= Level::Warn`.
